_doc: MultiLineSendPolicy (QuipMac/Services/MultiLineSendPolicy.swift) for send_text. input: text (as received from the phone), cliKind (claude|codex|grok|shell|cursor), terminalApp (the Mac host: Terminal|iTerm2|Claude), pressReturn (what the phone asked). expect: normalizedText = text with ONE trailing line break removed (this is what gets injected); isMultiLine = normalizedText still contains a line break; lineCount = lines in normalizedText, empty ones included; route = pasteText|sendText (Mac-specific injection path); pressReturn = whether Return is pressed after; latencySuffix = what latency.log gains (non-empty only when a requested Return was dropped; counts only, never text). A line break is a Swift Character with isNewline: LF, VT (U+000B), FF (U+000C), CR, NEL (U+0085), LS (U+2028), PS (U+2029), and CRLF, which is ONE Character, so it counts as one break. The Windows host (every terminal a shell in phase 1) is held to the shell cases in Terminal/iTerm2: multi-line never gets a Return. Expected values are written by the Swift test (QUIP_WRITE_VECTORS=1), never by hand. On Windows, spec 5.4 applies first: multi-line text to cmd.exe or a shell not proven safe is refused with an error before this policy runs, inner line breaks to PowerShell are sent as Shift+Enter (M0 ruled out clipboard paste: in Windows Terminal one Return ran only one of two pasted lines), and route has no meaning there.
